[WIP] How the project runs from its sources to these pages, and four places where the plan met the data and changed. The shorter chart of the method is on the [Methods and limitations](methods.qmd) page.

:::: {.fig-wide}
::: {.fig-light}
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-alt: "Flowchart of the whole project, top to bottom. Four streams start from sources. ENSO index from NOAA: every winter since 1950 is classified; the question whether ONI is still the index to use is answered no, NOAA made RONI its official index, so RONI classifies winters and ONI is kept as a check. ERA5-Land and snow stations: regional means weighted by latitude; the question whether El Niño dries the northern winter is answered only faintly in the Pacific Northwest and BC, so snowpack and snowfall share are tested too. Region boundaries: five regions at first; the question whether five cover it is answered no, so Alaska and Yukon were added, making seven. Fire perimeters from MTBS, WFIGS and CNFDB: burned area per season; the question whether one Canadian source holds up is answered no, Parks Canada polygons are missing for six years, so four Alberta seasons are flagged and NBAC is run as a check. The four streams meet in one region by year table. Below it: the pre-registered tests, run once, fed from the side by the analysis plan frozen before any fire data was read; the result tables, never edited after the run; figures and tables written by code; the site, which reads only those; and the site's five pages."
from IPython.display import SVG
SVG(filename="../results/figures/project_flow.svg")
```
:::
